summary: The agent component is the loop driver: a budget-guarded state machine (Planning -> Executing -> ErrorRecovery -> Completed/Failed) implemented by AgentLoop over AgentState. run_task resets loop state, seeds a TaskCheckpoint and Plan, then iterates turns that call the LLM, collect ToolCalls, execute them, and advance state until the task completes or the iteration/token/wall budget is exhausted. It owns iteration counting, valid state transitions, recovery hints, plan-mode gating, and cumulative budget accounting.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/agent/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in loop_control.rs AgentState/AgentLoop, task_runner.rs run_task, plan_mode.rs Plan/PlanStep, recovery.rs, and mod.rs budget derivation.

examples.title: Seed the state machine at Planning
examples.intent: Guarantee every task starts in a known Planning state with a zeroed iteration counter.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentLoop::new sets state=Planning and iteration=0; run_task calls reset_for_task so a queued follow-up cannot inherit the previous task's counter and trip max-iterations immediately.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User drags the Planning node from the palette onto the canvas as the loop's single entry point; it snaps to the start anchor.
touch_interaction.visual: Planning node renders cyan with a slow breathing pulse to signal it is armed but not yet consuming budget.

examples.mini_scenario: A new task arrives; run_task calls reset_for_task, the loop lands in Planning, and the counter reads 0 before the first LLM turn.
examples.pitfall: Reusing an Agent for a follow-up without reset_for_task carries stale iteration counts and can fail the new task on turn one.

examples.title: Advance only through valid transitions
examples.intent: Prevent illegal jumps between loop states (e.g. Completed back to Executing).
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: transition_to consults is_valid_transition; an InvalidStateTransition error is returned rather than corrupting the state, so the state graph stays a legal DAG of Planning->Executing->(ErrorRecovery)->Completed/Failed.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a finger edge from one state node to another; the canvas rejects and snaps back any edge that is not in the allowed transition set.
touch_interaction.visual: A legal edge draws solid green; an illegal edge flashes red and dissolves with a shake.

examples.mini_scenario: After Completed, a stray attempt to re-enter Executing is refused by is_valid_transition and the loop stays terminal.
examples.pitfall: Bypassing transition_to via set_state's expect() will panic on an invalid edge instead of surfacing a recoverable error.

examples.title: Count iterations without charging Planning
examples.intent: Give the model max_iterations execution turns plus one free Planning turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: next_state increments iteration only when the state is not Planning; once iteration exceeds max_iterations it forces AgentState::Failed with 'Max iterations exceeded'.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User pinches the Executing node to reveal a ring gauge showing iterations consumed against the max_iterations budget.
touch_interaction.visual: The gauge fills amber as iterations climb and turns red on the turn that forces Failed.

examples.mini_scenario: On the turn where iteration crosses max_iterations, next_state returns Failed and the loop halts cleanly instead of spinning forever.
examples.pitfall: Incrementing the counter during Planning would silently rob the model of one execution turn.

examples.title: Warn before the iteration wall
examples.intent: Let the model wrap up before it is force-failed for running out of turns.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: approaching_limit_warning and approaching_limit_band inject a system Message when the loop nears max_iterations, nudging the model toward a final answer while it still has budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Executing node opens a threshold slider that sets when the wrap-up warning fires.
touch_interaction.visual: The node grows an amber warning badge that pulses faster as the loop approaches the band.

examples.mini_scenario: At band 2 the loop injects 'you are nearly out of turns; finalize now' and the model produces its answer on the next turn.
examples.pitfall: Warning too late (only at the last turn) leaves no room for the model to actually finish.

examples.title: Perceive the task and build the L1 tree
examples.intent: Ground the loop in the repository before any planning happens.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_task sets modality from the task, builds the L1 project tree, and for Review modality auto-loads L2 skeletons so the model perceives structure without reading 100+ files one by one.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User spreads two fingers over the Perceive node to expand it into the layered L1/L2 context map view.
touch_interaction.visual: The node blooms into a nested tree; loaded skeletons glow, unloaded ones stay dim.

examples.mini_scenario: A 'review the config module' task classifies as Review modality, auto-loads skeletons, and the model plans against real structure.
examples.pitfall: Skipping the L1 build makes the model blind-read files, burning budget on discovery it could have perceived up front.

examples.title: Compose a Plan of PlanSteps
examples.intent: Turn the task into an ordered, trackable list of steps.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Plan::add_step appends PlanSteps; next_pending_step drives which step the loop tackles, and completed_count/is_complete tell the control layer when the plan is exhausted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Reason node opens an editable step list the user can reorder by dragging rows.
touch_interaction.visual: Each PlanStep is a chip: grey pending, blue in-progress, green done, red failed.

examples.mini_scenario: The planner emits steps 'find files', 'implement', 'cargo_check', 'cargo_test'; the loop pulls next_pending_step each turn.
examples.pitfall: A plan with no completion check lets the loop mark done before is_complete is actually true.

examples.title: Gate execution behind plan approval
examples.intent: Hold the loop in a read-only planning phase until the user approves.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: toggle_plan_mode / is_in_plan_mode keep the loop from mutating; approve_plan flips is_plan_approved so Executing can begin, converting plan mode into an explicit control checkpoint.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A padlock badge sits on the edge into Executing; tapping it once toggles approval and unlocks the edge.
touch_interaction.visual: Locked edge is dashed grey; on approval it turns solid green and the padlock springs open.

examples.mini_scenario: In plan mode the model drafts a Plan, the user taps approve, is_plan_approved becomes true, and only then does the loop start editing.
examples.pitfall: Letting mutating tools run while is_in_plan_mode is still true defeats the entire dry-run guarantee.

examples.title: Mark step progress as the loop runs
examples.intent: Keep an honest record of which steps are in-flight, done, or failed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PlanStep::mark_in_progress/mark_done/mark_failed update StepStatus so progress reporting and the completion gate reason over real per-step state rather than turn counts.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks a step chip right to mark done or left to mark failed, mirroring what the loop records automatically.
touch_interaction.visual: A right flick fills the chip green with a checkmark; a left flick fills red with a reason tooltip.

examples.mini_scenario: After cargo_test passes, the loop calls mark_done on that PlanStep and completed_count ticks up.
examples.pitfall: Marking a step done before its verifying tool succeeds inflates completed_count and can trigger premature completion.

examples.title: Divert into ErrorRecovery on failure
examples.intent: Route recoverable failures through a dedicated recovery state instead of failing the whole task.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A failing tool transitions Executing -> ErrorRecovery { error }; is_valid_transition permits ErrorRecovery -> Executing so the loop can retry, or ErrorRecovery -> Failed if unrecoverable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a recovery loop edge from Executing to the ErrorRecovery node and back, forming a visible retry cycle.
touch_interaction.visual: The ErrorRecovery node glows orange and the retry edge animates a return arrow when a retry is chosen.

examples.mini_scenario: A flaky network tool fails, the loop enters ErrorRecovery, emits a hint, then transitions back to Executing to retry.
examples.pitfall: Allowing unlimited ErrorRecovery->Executing cycles without a counter turns recovery into an infinite retry loop.

examples.title: Build an error-recovery hint for the model
examples.intent: Feed the model a concrete next-step suggestion instead of a bare error.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: build_error_recovery_hint turns a tool name and error into guidance (e.g. connection may self-heal next attempt) injected as a Message so the next reason turn adapts rather than repeats.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the ErrorRecovery node reveals the generated hint text bubble that will be injected.
touch_interaction.visual: A speech-bubble badge fades in over the node carrying the hint preview.

examples.mini_scenario: After a failed http_request the loop injects 'the connection may recover automatically; retry once' and the model retries deliberately.
examples.pitfall: Injecting a generic hint for a deterministic error (bad path) wastes a turn re-attempting the same doomed call.

examples.title: Detect and break a stuck loop
examples.intent: Stop the loop from repeating the same fruitless action forever.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: consecutive_no_tool_call_turns and GuardCounters (no-action prompts, mutation-gate rejections, prefill 400 breaker) escalate pressure and can force Failed, converting silent spinning into a bounded, observable stop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the control hub surfaces the guard-counter dials for no-action, mutation-gate, and prefill breakers.
touch_interaction.visual: Each dial reddens as its counter climbs; crossing the threshold flashes a stop icon.

examples.mini_scenario: Three consecutive no-tool-call turns raise the guard, inject a firmer directive, and if ignored transition the loop to Failed.
examples.pitfall: Setting the guard threshold too low kills legitimately slow reasoning turns that just happen not to call a tool.

examples.title: Latch the wall-clock budget
examples.intent: Give the whole loop a hard wall-clock ceiling that resume cannot reset.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: budget_elapsed_secs sums prior_elapsed_secs with the current run, so max_wall_secs is measured against total lifetime; the loop stops when the deadline passes regardless of state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User rotates a two-finger dial on the foundation node to set the wall-clock ceiling for the entire loop.
touch_interaction.visual: A clock ring drains as wall time is consumed and turns red when the deadline is latched shut.

examples.mini_scenario: A task resumed from checkpoint keeps its original deadline because budget_elapsed_secs carries prior_elapsed_secs forward.
examples.pitfall: Resetting elapsed time on resume would hand the loop an unlimited effective budget and break the ceiling.

examples.title: Derive the context/token budget at startup
examples.intent: Fit the conversation inside the model's real context window before the first turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Agent::new calls config.derive_context_budget to compute max_context_tokens and reserved output, sizing the compressor to the usable conversation budget rather than the raw output cap.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the foundation node fans out three bars: total context, safety margin, and usable conversation budget.
touch_interaction.visual: The usable-budget bar glows green; the safety margin is shown hatched and reserved.

examples.mini_scenario: At startup the loop reserves 20% margin and derives max_context_tokens, so the compressor keeps turns inside the window.
examples.pitfall: Sizing the compressor to token_budget (the output cap) instead of max_context_tokens overflows the real window.

examples.title: Compress history to reclaim budget
examples.intent: Free conversation budget mid-loop without losing task continuity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: compact_micro/compact_auto/compact_full shrink the Message history via the CompressionOrchestrator, letting the loop keep iterating instead of dying on context overflow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the history strip collapses old turns into a single summary card while keeping recent turns expanded.
touch_interaction.visual: Collapsed turns fold into a stacked card with a token-saved badge; recent turns stay crisp.

examples.mini_scenario: As budget nears the ceiling the loop runs compact_auto, folds early turns to a summary, and continues executing.
examples.pitfall: Compacting away the task statement or key evidence strands the model with no anchor for the remaining work.

examples.title: Snapshot progress into a TaskCheckpoint
examples.intent: Persist enough loop state that the task can resume after interruption.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_task creates a TaskCheckpoint holding current_step, current_iteration, messages, tool_calls, and cumulative budget; the loop updates it so continue_execution can pick up mid-flight.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the control hub drops a checkpoint pin onto the timeline capturing the current loop state.
touch_interaction.visual: A pin badge with the step/iteration numbers materializes and pulses once to confirm the save.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-task the loop writes a checkpoint; after a crash, continue_execution restores step and iteration and resumes.
examples.pitfall: Overwriting the checkpoint's task_description on a reused Agent points the completion gate at the wrong task.

examples.title: Enforce explicit required tools before answering
examples.intent: Refuse to finish until tools the task explicitly named have actually run.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_task extracts explicit_task_tools, activates them, and appends a directive so the completion path blocks a final answer until each required tool has succeeded.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws mandatory edges from named tool nodes into a 'required' collar around the completion node.
touch_interaction.visual: Each required tool edge is amber and thick until its tool succeeds, then it turns green and thins.

examples.mini_scenario: A task says 'use cargo_test'; the loop activates it and will not emit a final answer until cargo_test has passed.
examples.pitfall: Marking a required tool satisfied on a failed call lets the loop answer without the evidence it was told to gather.

examples.title: Escalate to careful/rigor mode
examples.intent: Slow the loop down and add verification when outcomes look risky.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: should_enter_rigor inspects a ResolutionOutcome and, when it warrants, injects careful_mode_directive so subsequent reason turns are more methodical and completion requires verification.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the Reason node with two fingers dials rigor from fast to careful, adding verify sub-steps.
touch_interaction.visual: At higher rigor the node deepens to indigo and grows an extra verification sub-node.

examples.mini_scenario: After a shaky resolution the loop enters rigor, injects the careful directive, and demands verification before completing.
examples.pitfall: Entering rigor on every minor hiccup makes routine tasks crawl and burns the wall-clock budget.

examples.title: Verify before declaring Completed
examples.intent: Block the Completed transition until the work is actually verified.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: completion_requires_verification and the baseline-dirty capture make the Executing -> Completed transition conditional on evidence, so the loop cannot self-declare success on unverified edits.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A checkmark gate sits on the edge into Completed; it stays greyed until verification evidence lands, then becomes tappable.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate icon is a hollow check while unverified and fills solid green once evidence passes.

examples.mini_scenario: The model claims done, but the completion gate holds the loop in Executing until cargo_test evidence appears.
examples.pitfall: Counting pre-existing uncommitted changes as new work lets the gate pass on edits the loop never made.

examples.title: Classify the terminal failure mode
examples.intent: Record why a loop ended so the outcome is diagnosable, not just 'failed'.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: last_run_failure_mode captures a FailureMode (budget stop, max iterations, unrecoverable error) on the terminal transition, and terminal_event_emitted guards against double-emitting the end event.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a terminal node reveals its labeled failure/success reason and the single terminal event it emitted.
touch_interaction.visual: Failed nodes carry a red tag with the mode label; Completed nodes carry a green success tag.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop hits the wall-clock ceiling; last_run_failure_mode is set to a budget stop and exactly one terminal event fires.
examples.pitfall: Emitting the terminal event twice (missing the terminal_event_emitted latch) confuses downstream listeners.

examples.title: Reset cleanly for the next queued task
examples.intent: Ensure a reused Agent starts the next task with no residue from the last.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_task clears failed-tool attempts, no-action prompt state, failure-mode counters, required tools, cumulative token/cost usage, and dirty-path baseline before the new loop begins.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks the whole canvas downward to sweep the previous run's counters and badges off before the next task drops in.
touch_interaction.visual: Old badges fade and slide away; the state graph resets to the single breathing Planning node.

examples.mini_scenario: A queued follow-up task starts; run_task wipes cumulative usage and counters so its budget and guards start from zero.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting to reset cumulative_token_usage bleeds the previous task's spend into the next task's budget accounting.
